sourceUse: Part B adopted 9 June 2026 establishes 60 EC year one, 48 EC core plus 12 EC Philosophy, 42 EC open electives and 18 EC thesis. Appendix 1 lists the two equal-credit specialisations. The unfiltered catalogue node aggregates both 36 EC lists into 96 EC in year two. Selecting one programme path gives the controlling 24+36 EC. Cultural Information Studies comes first in the official list and is selected without reference to UCR overlap. The Cultural Information Studies appendix table uses the title Digital Methods and Research Practices. Article B4.7, the dated scheme and the individual entry identify Digital Methods and Information Analytics for the 12 EC common unit at the same blocks. Media Aesthetics is limited to documented switchers and not counted in the ordinary first year. The catalogue labels academic writing, literacy and tutoring at zero EC.

progression.yearOne: The autumn foundation in Living Information, Analysing Digital Culture and media practice precedes Media Research and Doing Media Studies 2. Academic writing is associated with Media Research without additional credits.
progression.yearTwo: The dated catalogue and B4.4 require positive BSA for progression. Analysing Digital Culture and Doing Media Studies 2 prepare for Digital Methods, Introduction to Digital Humanities and Archives. The block-1 Introduction to Digital Humanities precedes Coding in block 4 and the lab in blocks 5–6. Philosophy 1 in block 4 precedes Philosophy 2 in block 5. The unselected New Media direction includes New Media Theory, Digital Practices, Data Journalism and Histories of Digital Culture.
progression.yearThree: Appendix 1 allocates 30 EC open in autumn and 12 EC open in spring. The 18 EC seminar and thesis are scheduled in spring in the ordinary route. Entry requires passing the mandatory first and second years, except Archives, Information and Society on this route, or Digital Practices for the other specialisation. The seminar develops research plans and leads to the supervised independent thesis.
progression.openChoice: Dated electives guidance permits a minor, electives, approved study elsewhere or a placement. External courses require Examination Board permission. Introductory electives normally have a 12 EC cap, subject to the listed minor and language exceptions.
